content: Bag Balm is a topical salve that was originally developed to alleviate irritation on the udders of cows. Despite its original purpose, it is widely used by humans to treat chapped and irritated skin. The product is commonly available in drugstores and ski resorts and has also become popular as a soothing agent for skin after receiving tattoos. Bag Balm is manufactured by the Dairy Association Co., with production facilities located in Lyndonville, Vermont, and Rock Island, Quebec. The product is easily recognizable due to its iconic 10-ounce green tins, which feature a cow's head and red clovers on the lid. It has been in continuous production since 1899. The active ingredient in Bag Balm is 8-hydroxyquinoline sulfate at a concentration of 0.3%, which serves as an antiseptic. This is combined with a base of petrolatum and lanolin, which provide moisturizing and protective properties. Historically, Bag Balm contained 0.002% mercury in its formulation. This earlier version was noted for its superior efficacy in treating infections, with reports of it being able to completely resolve infected wounds overnight. However, the mercury content has since been removed from the product.
